en: Conditioned by a state that is neither with-root nor wholesome, a state that is with-root and wholesome arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of root; ... pe ... one in the case of non-disappearance.

Conditioned by a state that is neither with-root nor unwholesome, a state that is with-root and unwholesome arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. One in the case of root; three in the case of object; one in the case of predominance; ... pe ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is neither with-root nor indeterminate, a state that is without-root and indeterminate arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted nor indeterminate, a state that is neither-rooted and indeterminate arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on states that are both not accompanied by roots and not indeterminate, and states that are neither-rooted and not indeterminate, a state that is neither-rooted and indeterminate arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition, three; with respect to predominance-condition, one …pe… with respect to non-disappearance-condition, three. Conditioned by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya): A state that is neither root (na-hetu), nor non-root (na-ahetuka), and not wholesome (nakusala) is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is wholesome (kusala), accompanied by roots (sahetuka), and whose roots are not themselves [the condition for it] (na-hetu).

A state that is neither root, nor non-root, and not wholesome is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is wholesome, accompanied by roots, and whose roots are themselves [the condition for it] (hetu), as well as for a state that is wholesome, accompanied by roots, and whose roots are not themselves [the condition for it] (sahetuka).
A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of object-condition … three.
A state that is neither rootless nor non-root, and is not wholesome, is a condition for a state that is both rooted and with root, and is wholesome, by way of object-condition … three.

States that are neither roots nor rootless and are not wholesome, and states that are neither roots nor rootless and are not wholesome, are conditions for a state that is both rooted and with root, and is wholesome, by way of object-condition … three.
With respect to object, predominance, and decisive support, there are nine [ways].

A state that is neither root nor rootless and is not unwholesome is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is both root and accompanied by roots and is unwholesome. With respect to object, predominance, and decisive support, there are nine [ways].
A state that is neither root nor rootless and is not indeterminate is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is both root and accompanied by roots and is indeterminate.
Dhamma is related to dhamma by object-condition ... three. With respect to object: nine (by) predominance, proximity, contiguity, decisive support;
three (by) kamma; nine (by) absence and disappearance.
